Done

What is a "platform specific service"?  Why aren't we doing this in phosphor-host-ipmid?

How is this hosted upstream?

+1. We should avoid designs that depend on downstream implementations. From the current design, it seems this feature would break if the platform-specific service is not upstream. We also cannot allow partial implementations in bios-settings-mgr, as that would result in dead code—unused, inaccessible, and ultimately confusing for users and developers alike.

We have a service that monitors GPIO changes to detect when the BIOS has booted, which signals the BMC. Since each system may have different methods for detecting BIOS boot completion, why do we need to use IPMI commands for this purpose? Would it be sufficient to simply update the BootProgressLastUpdate attribute instead?
@manojkiran.eda@gmail.com - This design depends on the use of BootProgressLastUpdate and not on the platform-specific service. Each platform has its own way to detect the host booting; the service needs to update the BootProgressLastUpdate fla, and this is generic for all platforms.

As per the quoted design document for boot-progress:

```
It is the responsibility the phosphor-state-manager to update the BootProgressLastUpdate property on D-Bus when it sees BootProgress updated.
```

I don't think directly updating the `BootProgressLastUpdate` by any other service apart from phosphor-state-manager is acceptable upstream.

@manojkiran.eda@gmail.com - The phosphor-state manager only provides a set method. In the actual implementation, it does not change the value.
Also, I think that a host boot is platform-specific, so it needs to be changed by another service.

I am not sure about that, I believe state management owner @geissonator@yahoo.com should be a part of this review. As far as the set method - I believe that should have been a read only property in the first place. Not sure why it is made read/write.

I still think updating the bootprogresslastupdate by other services apart from state-manager is wrong.

You know this got me digging through the PSM code and it doesn't look like I ever added support for BootProgressLastUpdate! I'm not sure why. I see phosphor-host-ipmid went ahead and just added support for it (my initial design was ipmi/pldm would own updating it but review comments changed that and moved the responsibility to PSM). So I need to add this support to PSM. If your platform uses PSM then PSM needs to be in control of this property. If you don't use PSM, then you can write whatever you like to the property.
PSM code change up at https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-state-manager/+/84425
Change the design - the BIOS booting signal will be notified by the change of BootProgress to "PrimaryProcInit"
Is there a reason phosphor-watchdog isn't involved here?  Doesn't it already handle some timeouts?

Since this involves the logic and attributes of the BIOS settings manager that are needed to determine whether the timeout should be canceled or not, how can we integrate phosphor-watchdog in this scenario?
This is not acceptable.
Done

added

Added more details. However, testing will be conducted directly on BMC by verifying the attributes.

Are any of these applications upstreamed in openbmc ? Does this feature benefit any other platform apart from nvidia platforms ?
@manojkiran.eda@gmail.com - I will remove the line about the benefit of the boot detection. Other platforms will benefit from the use of the timeout defined in the IPMI spec.
we need to also document, the current mechanism for setting the boot flags ? and what's the significance of bios-settings-mgr application in this process

BootProgressLastUpdate - is meant to understand how long we are at a particular state of the boot.

So we plan to just check for one property change event to cancel the timer ? and leave the rest of the events ?
If the enable flag is `false` - how does bios consume this value ? is it via redfish ? or via IPMI ?  can you add that detail as well ?
@manojkiran.eda@gmail.com - it is consumed directly from the D-bus. I have added this to the doc
I don't think BIOS understands dbus right ?
Yes, it can read from IPMI or ReFish -added it to the doc
why ? if it is implemented in IPMI ? can't it be shown in redfish ?
@manojkiran.eda@gmail.com - The redfish does not define a timeout property. Once it is added (not that I'm aware of this plan), it can use this design.

As per the design document quoted above :

1. Ensure the BootProgress and BootProgressLastUpdate properties are updated appropriately in both IPMI and PLDM based stacks
2. It is the responsibility of the IPMI or PLDM implementation to update the BootProgress property on D-Bus
3. **It is the responsibility the phosphor-state-manager to update the BootProgressLastUpdate property on D-Bus when it sees BootProgress updated**

This completely violates #3. Doesn't nvidia use phsopshor-state-manager repo ?

@manojkiran.eda@gmail.com
1.  BootProgress and BootProgressLastUpdate - there is one property -BootProgressLastUpdate. What do you mean by "updated appropriately in both IPMI and PLDM based stacks"? This will be used only in the bios-manager to know that the host booted.
2. BootProgressLastUpdate - it is the platform's responsibility to update this D-Bus. 
3. The phosphor-state-manager only gives get and set methods. This property is not updated from BootProgress. Nvidia uses this repository.
https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/34fde7c0b23a322dd723d4f4998b48f43f349feb/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/State/Boot/Progress.interface.yaml#L11
